contact_edits.before: Hughson and Ouimette get their laughs cleanly on the lines. Bruce Dow, in the star role of Pseudolus, acts fussily around his; he only comes into focus when he duets with Ouimette on the reprise of Lovely, the comic love-duet (already a hoot when the young 'uns do it). Most spectacularly miscalculated is Dan Chameroy's Miles Gloriosus ( "braggart soldier") who should be impregnably self-satisfied and terrifying, but is here made of jelly. But the actor hardly stands a chance in a production that has a single chariot wheel careening across the stage before his entrance, thus undercutting his immortal first line, "Stand aside, everyone! I take large steps!" Lycus is an underwritten role but Cliff Saunders' decision to play him as an epicene eccentric rather than a mercenary man of business is not a happy one. His non-speaking merchandise includes regular Stratford adornment Sara Topham, who may not be playing Medea later this week, as the song says, but was once a memorable Cassandra, and is obviously having a ball here. They've cut Pretty Little Picture, which is unforgivable, but they're not the first. The show remains irresistible. It all turns out all right. It has to. - A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum is in repertory through Nov. 1. Call 1-800-567-1600 or visit stratfordfestival.cafor tickets and information.
